title: Lost in the Mountains
summary: Two friends hiking in the mountains take a wrong turn, get separated from their group, and use problem-solving and hiking skills to find their way back safely.
poll: Staying calm is more important than being strong when something goes wrong outdoors.

versions.title: Lost in the Mountains
versions.text:
Yusuf and his friend Khalid go on a class hike. Their teacher leads the group.

The trail splits into two paths. The boys stop to tie a shoe. The group walks ahead.

The boys take the wrong path. Soon, Yusuf looks around. Where is everyone? he asks.

Khalid feels scared too. They are lost on the mountain.

Stop. Let's think, says Yusuf. He stays calm. Do not run, he says.

Khalid sees a mark on a rock. Look! A trail mark! They follow the marks.

They hear a whistle. It is their teacher! They blow their own whistle back.

The group hears it. They walk toward the sound. Soon, they see their friends.

We are so glad to see you! says their teacher.

The boys tell how they stayed calm. The group walks down the mountain together.

Yusuf and his best friend Khalid join their class on a mountain hike. Their teacher leads the whole group up a trail.

Partway up, the trail splits into two paths. Yusuf and Khalid stop to tie a loose shoelace. The rest of the group walks ahead without them.

The two boys take the wrong path by mistake. Soon, Yusuf looks around. Where did everyone go? he asks, his voice shaking.

Khalid feels scared too. The boys slowly see that they are lost on the mountain.

Stop. Let's think, says Yusuf, trying to stay calm. He remembers what their teacher taught. Stay on the trail. Never run into the trees.

Khalid sees a painted mark on a big rock. Look! A trail mark! The boys follow the marks slowly.

Soon, they hear a loud whistle. It must be their teacher! The boys blow their own whistle back, three short blasts.

The group hears the whistle and walks toward the sound. Soon, Yusuf and Khalid see their friends.

We are so glad to see you both! their teacher says, hugging them.

The boys explain how they stayed calm and used the trail marks. The whole group walks back down the mountain together, tired but happy.

versions.title: Lost in the Mountains
versions.text:
Yusuf and his best friend Khalid joined their class on an exciting overnight mountain hike, a trip they had looked forward to for months. Their teacher led the whole group up a rocky trail toward a distant, hazy summit.

Partway up the mountain, the main trail unexpectedly split into two paths that looked almost the same. Yusuf and Khalid stopped for a moment to tie a loose shoelace. The rest of the group walked on ahead, never noticing the two boys had fallen behind.

When they stood back up, the boys took the wrong path without noticing their mistake. After walking for several minutes, Yusuf looked around and frowned, feeling disoriented among the unfamiliar rocks and trees. Where did everyone go? he asked, his voice shaking with worry he could not hide.

Khalid felt nervous too, glancing at the silent trees around them. The two boys slowly realized that they were now completely lost somewhere on the mountain, far from any landmark they knew.

Stop. Let's think clearly before we do anything, said Yusuf, forcing himself not to panic. He remembered what their teacher had carefully taught the class. We should stay on the trail we can see. We should never run off into the trees.

Khalid suddenly noticed a small painted mark on a large gray rock, almost hidden under some moss. Look! A trail mark! he shouted, pointing at it. From that landmark on, the two boys followed the trail marks slowly and carefully.

Soon, they heard a loud whistle echo through the quiet mountains. It had to be their worried teacher, searching for them! The boys quickly pulled out their own whistle and signaled back, three short blasts, exactly as they had practiced.

The group heard the answering whistle and began walking toward the sound, calling the boys' names. Before long, Yusuf and Khalid spotted their relieved classmates through the trees.

We are so relieved to see you both safe! their teacher exclaimed, pulling them into a tight hug.

Yusuf and Khalid explained exactly how they had stayed calm, followed the trail marks, and used their whistle to signal clearly for help, instead of trying to retrace their steps alone. The whole group walked back down the mountain together, tired but entirely safe and happy.

Partway up the mountain, the main trail unexpectedly split into two paths that looked almost identical. Yusuf and Khalid stopped for a moment to retie a loose shoelace. The rest of the group walked steadily ahead, never noticing the two boys had quietly fallen behind.

When they finally stood back up, the boys took the wrong path, not noticing their mistake until too late. After walking for several minutes, Yusuf looked around and frowned, feeling disoriented among the unfamiliar rocks and trees. Where did everyone go? he asked, his voice shaking with worry he could not hide.

Khalid felt nervous too, glancing anxiously at the silent trees pressing close around them. The two boys slowly realized that they were now completely lost somewhere on the mountain, far from any landmark they recognized.

Stop. Let's think clearly before we do anything, said Yusuf, forcing himself not to panic despite his racing heart. He remembered what their teacher had carefully taught the class. We should stay right here on the trail we can still see. We should never run off blindly into the trees.

Khalid suddenly noticed a small painted mark on a large gray rock, almost hidden beneath patches of moss. Look! A trail mark! he shouted excitedly, pointing at it. From that landmark onward, the two boys followed the trail marks slowly and carefully.

Soon, they heard a loud whistle echo sharply through the quiet mountains. It had to be their worried teacher, searching for them! The boys quickly pulled out their own emergency whistle and signaled back firmly, three short blasts, exactly as practiced.

The rest of the group heard the answering whistle and immediately began walking briskly toward the sound, calling both boys' names. Before long, Yusuf and Khalid spotted their relieved classmates through a gap in the dense trees.

We are so deeply relieved to see you both safe! their teacher exclaimed, pulling them into a tight, grateful hug.

Yusuf and Khalid carefully explained how they had managed to stay calm, followed the trail marks, and used their whistle wisely, rather than trying to retrace their steps alone. The whole group walked back down the mountain together, tired but entirely safe and happy about how the day had ended.

versions.title: Lost in the Mountains
versions.text:
Yusuf and his closest friend Khalid joined their class on an exciting overnight mountain hike, a trip they had eagerly anticipated for several months, ever since their teacher first announced the plan weeks earlier during an ordinary class meeting. Their teacher led the group up a rocky, winding trail that climbed steadily toward a distant, hazy summit above the drifting clouds.

Partway up the mountain, the main trail unexpectedly diverged into two paths that appeared almost indistinguishable, with no obvious marker indicating either direction clearly. Yusuf and Khalid paused momentarily to retie a loose shoelace that kept slipping across the uneven, rocky terrain beneath their boots. Meanwhile, the rest of the group continued steadily ahead, never noticing that the two boys had quietly fallen behind on the narrowing trail.

When they finally stood back up, the boys inadvertently took the wrong path, not recognizing their error until it was already far too late to easily retrace their steps. After navigating uncertainly for several minutes, Yusuf surveyed his surroundings and frowned, visibly disoriented by the unfamiliar rocks and trees encircling them. Where did everyone go? he asked, his voice trembling noticeably with mounting worry he could not quite manage to conceal from his friend.

Khalid felt anxious too, glancing warily at the silent trees pressing closely around them from every direction, their shadows lengthening steadily as the afternoon wore on. The two boys slowly, almost reluctantly, recognized that they were now thoroughly disoriented somewhere on the mountain, far from any recognizable landmark.

Stop. Let's think clearly before we attempt anything else, said Yusuf, forcing himself to remain calm and retain his composure despite his racing, pounding heart hammering within his chest. He recalled precisely what their teacher had carefully instilled in the entire class before embarking on this hike that morning. We ought to remain exactly where we can still see a clear trail. We should never, under any circumstance, dash off blindly into the surrounding woods, however frightened we might feel.

Khalid suddenly noticed a small painted mark upon a large gray boulder nearby, almost entirely concealed beneath a thick patch of green moss clinging to the stone's surface. Look! A trail mark! he exclaimed excitedly, gesturing directly at it. From that landmark onward, the two boys followed the painted markers methodically, navigating carefully back toward a recognizable trail.

Before long, they heard a resonant whistle echo sharply through the quiet, towering peaks surrounding them. It had to be their worried teacher, searching frantically for the two missing boys somewhere nearby! Without wasting a single precious second, they swiftly produced their own emergency whistle and signaled back firmly, three short blasts, exactly as they had rehearsed together many times before.

The remainder of the group detected the answering whistle and immediately commenced walking briskly toward the sound, calling both boys' names loudly across the steep mountainside. Before long, Yusuf and Khalid glimpsed their visibly relieved classmates through a narrow gap in the dense, leafy canopy.

We are so profoundly relieved to see you both safe and entirely sound! their teacher exclaimed, pulling them both into a tight, grateful embrace.

Yusuf and Khalid carefully recounted exactly how they had managed to remain composed, followed the painted trail markers methodically, and deployed their whistle judiciously to signal clearly for urgently needed assistance. The whole group descended the mountain together afterward, exhausted yet entirely secure, and the two friends were profoundly relieved to finally reunite with their worried classmates.

We ought to remain exactly where we can still see a clear trail, and we should never, under any circumstance, dash off blindly into the surrounding woods, however disoriented or frightened we might feel in this uncertain moment.

Khalid suddenly noticed a small painted mark upon a large gray boulder nearby, almost entirely concealed beneath a thick patch of clinging moss. Look, a trail mark, he exclaimed, gesturing directly at it with a trembling finger. From that landmark onward, the two boys followed the painted markers methodically, navigating with great care and verifying each successive sign thoroughly before advancing confidently along the uncertain path that stretched ahead of them.

Before long, a resonant whistle echoed sharply through the quiet, towering peaks surrounding the narrow valley below; it had to be their worried teacher, searching frantically for the two missing boys somewhere amid the dense woods. Without wasting a single precious second, they swiftly produced their own emergency whistle and signaled back firmly, three short blasts, exactly as they had rehearsed many times before this challenging expedition had even begun.

The remainder of the group detected the answering whistle in the near distance and immediately began walking briskly toward the sound, calling both boys' names loudly across the steep mountainside. Before long, Yusuf and Khalid glimpsed their visibly relieved classmates through a narrow gap in the dense, leafy canopy just ahead on the winding trail. We are so profoundly relieved to see you both safe and entirely sound, their teacher exclaimed, pulling them both into a tight, grateful embrace without a moment's hesitation.

Yusuf and Khalid carefully recounted exactly how they had managed to remain composed, followed the painted trail markers methodically, and deployed their whistle judiciously to signal clearly for urgently needed assistance, demonstrating that calm, methodical navigation, rather than panic, had allowed them to reunite safely with their worried classmates. The whole group descended the mountain together afterward, exhausted yet entirely secure and genuinely, profoundly relieved about how the harrowing day had ultimately, thankfully concluded on a note of quiet triumph that none of them would soon forget, long after the initial memory of fear itself had gradually faded into a story worth retelling to younger hikers for years to come, a lasting testament to the enduring value of composure, methodical thinking, and the disciplined ability to navigate uncertainty without ever succumbing entirely to panic.

questions.stem: What is this story mostly about?

Two friends who get lost on a mountain trail and find their way back
A class that visits a museum on a school trip in the spring and sees old coins

questions.stem: Why do Yusuf and Khalid fall behind the group?

They climb a tree to look around
They stop to tie a shoelace
They fall asleep under a shady tree

The marks tell them the time of day

I would also look for trail marks, like Khalid found on the rock, to help me find my way. If I had a whistle, I would blow it so my group could hear me and come find me.

questions.stem: What does the boys' choice to use a whistle instead of shouting suggest about their training?

questions.stem: In what order do these events happen?

wrong.B: Tying the shoelace is what causes them to fall behind, so it comes first.

questions.stem: How does the author organize the events of the story?
options: By describing the whole hike from the teacher's point of view only, from start to end
By listing facts about mountain weather and the clouds that form on the peaks, one after another
By comparing two different mountains in detail, one tall and the other low, with a map

wrong.C: Only one mountain appears in the story.

MID.prompt: Explain how Yusuf and Khalid worked together to solve the problem of being lost. Use at least two details from the story.
checklist: I explained how the boys solved the problem.
I used at least two details from the story.
I organized my ideas in a clear order.
MID.modelAnswer: Yusuf and Khalid worked together calmly to solve their problem. When they first realized they were disoriented, Yusuf told Khalid to stop and think instead of panicking, which helped them avoid making the situation worse. Then Khalid spotted a landmark, a painted trail mark on a boulder, and the two boys followed similar marks carefully. Finally, they used their whistle to signal their location, which let their teacher and the rest of the group find them safely.

keyWords.definition: confused about where you are or which way to go

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses the central idea of the story?
options: A teacher decides the class should never hike again, because two of the students got lost for a day on the mountain.
A mountain hike is canceled because of dangerous weather, and the class goes back to school by bus.
Two friends, briefly separated from their hiking group, use composure and methodical skills to navigate back and reunite with their class.
Two disoriented hikers abandon their training and simply hope for someone to rescue them without trying to move or to think about where to go
questions.why: The story shows Yusuf and Khalid actively applying trail-reading and signaling skills, not merely hoping for luck, to reunite with their group.

wrong.A: The teacher is relieved, not opposed to future hikes.
wrong.B: No weather cancellation occurs in the story.
wrong.D: The boys apply their training deliberately rather than abandoning it.

questions.stem: What specific detail shows that the boys' separation from the group was accidental rather than intentional?
options: They were told by their teacher to wait behind, even though no one had actually given them that particular instruction
They ran ahead of the group on purpose
They decided together to explore a side trail
They paused briefly to retie a shoelace and did not notice the group moving on

wrong.A: The teacher never instructs them to wait.
wrong.B: They fall behind; they do not run ahead.
wrong.C: There is no mention of intentionally exploring.

questions.stem: How does Yusuf's internal state shift over the course of the story?
options: From bored on the hike to excited about the view
From angry at Khalid to forgiving him
From confident and composed at the start to permanently frightened and unable to function for the rest of the trip
From initial worry and a racing heart to deliberate composure and methodical problem-solving

wrong.B: Yusuf never expresses anger toward Khalid.

questions.stem: In the story, the word navigate most nearly means —

to measure the height of a mountain with a rope

options: It had nothing to do with their eventual survival
It was designed to make the hike more difficult
It was meant to teach them which plants are safe to eat in the desert
It was meant to prepare them for exactly this kind of emergency
questions.why: The boys directly rely on taught safety behaviors, trail marks, and the whistle, showing the training's purpose was preparation for emergencies.

wrong.B: The training helps, rather than complicates, their situation.

questions.stem: In what sequence did the key events of the story occur?
options: They signal with a whistle, they fall behind, they reunite, they get lost, they follow trail marks

questions.stem: What can readers infer from the fact that both the boys and the teacher used whistles to communicate?

The whistle was a toy the boys had brought for fun on the trip

questions.stem: Why does the author end the story with the boys explaining their methodical actions to the group?

To suggest the teacher should be blamed for the incident on the hill
To emphasize that calm, trained responses, not luck, led to their safe return

wrong.B: The ending focuses on the boys' actions, not geography.
wrong.C: The story does not blame the teacher.

HIGH.prompt: The poll says staying calm is more important than being strong when something goes wrong outdoors. Do you agree or disagree? Support your argument with evidence from the story about Yusuf and Khalid.
checklist: I stated a clear position on the poll statement.
I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that staying calm is more important than being strong when something goes wrong outdoors. Yusuf and Khalid were not rescued because of physical strength; they were reunited with their group because Yusuf kept his composure, told Khalid to stop and think, and the boys methodically followed trail markers and used their whistle to navigate back safely. Someone might argue that strength matters more on a difficult mountain climb, but even a very strong hiker who panics and runs blindly into the woods could become more lost and harder to find than two calm, disoriented boys who think carefully and signal for help.
